title: How to read an IRS page
subject: Money

text: How to read an IRS page
The page is usable if you can name three things: the tax year, who it applies to, and the limit.
If you cannot name all three, you do not have the number yet.
Look for 'tax year 2025' or 'returns filed in 2026'. Those are different phrases for related things.
A page can hold two years in one table. Read the column, not the headline.
Single is not head of household. Married filing jointly is not married filing separately.
A credit page will also split by number of children. The row for three children is not the row for none.
Find the limit, then the exception
The standard deduction is the usual filing line. Self-employment of $400 still requires a return under it.
EITC has an income limit and an investment-income limit. Missing either one disqualifies you. Read both.
A table has a column for tax year 2025 and a column for 2026. You are filing your 2025 return. Which column?

choices.label: 2025. That is the year you earned the money.
2026. That is the year you are sitting in.

text: Year, status, limit. Then the exception.
Write those four down before you type a number into a return. This module is a map. The page on IRS.gov is the territory.

notes: Example course. Teaches that figures change and how to read IRS.gov. Not tax advice.
